title: Council Conclusions on the 4th International Conference on Small Island Developing States (SIDS) 2024
executive_summary: The EU and its Member States welcome the 4th International Conference on Small Island Developing States (SIDS) in May 2024, emphasizing the theme "Charting the Course Toward Resilient Prosperity." Recognizing SIDS' vulnerability to climate change, environmental degradation, and socio-economic challenges, the EU commits to strengthening partnerships, supporting sustainable development, and advancing climate action. Key initiatives include endorsing the Multidimensional Vulnerability Index, enhancing digital transformation, and mobilizing innovative financing. The EU highlights its significant financial support, including over EUR 1.2 billion in bilateral aid and EUR 3.47 billion via the European Investment Bank. Cooperation frameworks like the new EU-OACPS Partnership Agreement and regional protocols aim to tailor support to SIDS' diverse needs. The EU also prioritizes disaster preparedness, ocean protection, and inclusive climate policies, pledging continued collaboration to implement the SAMOA Pathway and global commitments, ensuring SIDS' resilience and prosperity by 2034 and beyond.
characteristics: The EU strongly supports the 4th International Conference on SIDS (May 2024) and designates 2024 as the International Year of SIDS to mainstream their perspectives globally.
SIDS face disproportionate vulnerabilities due to small size, remoteness, and climate change impacts like sea-level rise, marine pollution, and biodiversity loss.
The EU collaborates closely with SIDS on climate action, sustainable blue economies, biodiversity protection, and digital transformation, emphasizing inclusive and equitable development.
The EU funds over EUR 1.2 billion in bilateral and multilateral aid to SIDS, supports disaster preparedness, and promotes private sector investment through initiatives like EFSD+.
The EU values partnerships with SIDS in UN climate negotiations, supports innovative financing, and fosters regional cooperation via the new EU-OACPS Partnership Agreement.
The EU commits to ongoing dialogue, capacity building, and cooperation on priority areas including climate change, energy, environment, and access to finance for SIDS development.

Political Actors: Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States

practical_applications: The EU and its Member States are funding more than EUR 1.2 billion in bilateral Official Development Assistance (ODA) and contributions through multilateral organizations to support SIDS in 2022.

Under the Global Gateway strategy, the EU and its Member States, as Team Europe, are partnering with SIDS through investments in digital, environment, climate and energy, transport, health, education, and research.

The EU funds strategic flagship initiatives benefiting SIDS, such as the Global Green Bonds Initiative, the ‘Green Blue Alliance for the Pacific’, and efforts to address the Sargassum algae plague in the Caribbean.

The European Investment Bank has provided EUR 3.47 billion in credit lines to local credit institutions in SIDS to support SMEs, infrastructure investments, and sectors including energy, services, health, education, agriculture, and fisheries.

The EU funds a EUR 35 billion program supporting African, Caribbean, and Pacific SIDS and coastal countries, including the Biospace program in the Caribbean, the Bioscape program in the Pacific, and support to the Critical Ecosystems Partnership Fund in the Western Indian Ocean.
The EU’s humanitarian Disaster Preparedness Programme has supported national authorities and local communities in SIDS for three decades to anticipate, respond, and recover from natural disasters.

A Memorandum of Understanding on Disaster Risk Management between the EU and Latin America and the Caribbean is to be signed in 2024, alongside launching a series of EU-LAC dialogues on disaster preparedness.
The EU supports the UN Secretary General’s ‘Early Warnings for All’ initiative, focusing on closing data gaps for weather and climate observations from SIDS and ensuring appropriate local warnings.

The EU works through the Digital for Development Hub (D4D Hub) to advance dialogue with partner regions, including the Caribbean and Pacific, to foster human-centered and sustainable digital transformation.
The European Fund for Sustainable Development Plus (EFSD+) provides guarantees to private sector investors through development financing institutions to leverage private sector investments in SIDS.

The new Partnership Agreement between the EU and the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS), signed in November 2023, offers a framework for cooperation on human rights, democracy, climate change, environment, and ocean governance, particularly relevant for SIDS.
The EU supports the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework in SIDS through Green Partnerships and cooperation assistance.
The EU and its Member States co-sponsored UN General Assembly Resolution 77/276 requesting an advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice on States’ obligations regarding climate change.
The EU is working closely with SIDS to conclude by the end of 2024 negotiations on an ambitious International Legally Binding Instrument to end plastic pollution.

The EU supports achieving land degradation neutrality by 2030 and welcomes COP16 to the UNCCD as a moment to accelerate action on land restoration, soil health, drought resilience, and green transition.

The EU and its Member States have pledged significant support to the new fund for assisting developing countries vulnerable to climate change loss and damage, as well as to existing funding arrangements.

The EU and its Member States collaborate with SIDS in developing and implementing ambitious Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) aligned with limiting global warming to 1.5°C, including economy-wide emission reduction targets.
The EU supports reform efforts of the International Financial Architecture and multilateral development banks, building on the Paris Pact for People and the Planet (4P) and the Bridgetown Agenda 2.0.
The EU promotes cooperation between SIDS and other islands, including the EU’s Outermost Regions (ORs) and Overseas Countries and Territories (OCTs), sharing common characteristics.
commitments: The EU and its Member States have pledged significant support to the new fund for assisting developing countries particularly vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change in responding to loss and damage (no specific amount or deadline given).
The EU and its Member States funded more than EUR 1.2 billion in bilateral Official Development Assistance (ODA) and contributions channeled through multilateral organizations to SIDS in 2022.
The European Investment Bank funded EUR 3.47 billion to SIDS as of December 2022, supporting SMEs, infrastructure, energy, services, health, education, agriculture, and fisheries.
The EU is funding a EUR 35 billion programme of support for African, Caribbean, and Pacific SIDS and coastal countries (no specific deadline given).
The EU will conclude a Memorandum of Understanding on Disaster Risk Management between the EU and Latin America and the Caribbean to be signed in 2024.
The EU aims to achieve land degradation neutrality by 2030.
The EU will work closely with SIDS towards concluding by the end of 2024 negotiations on an ambitious International Legally Binding Instrument to end plastic pollution.
The EU looks forward to the 4th International Conference on Financing for Development to be held in Spain in 2025.

The EU and its Member States will continue to strengthen collaboration with partners in developing and implementing ambitious Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) aligned with limiting global warming to 1.5°C (no specific deadline given).

The EU supports the swift ratification, entry into force, and implementation of the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, preparing for ambitious commitments at the 3rd UN Ocean Conference in June 2025.

kpi_list.kpi_text: The EU and its Member States together as Team Europe constitute the largest donor to the SIDS, funding more than EUR 1.2 billion in the form of bilateral ODA, and contributions channelled through multilateral organisations in 2022.
kpi_list.target_description: Provide more than EUR 1.2 billion in bilateral Official Development Assistance and multilateral contributions to SIDS
kpi_list.measurement_method: Financial disbursement and reporting of ODA contributions
kpi_list.responsible_entity: European Union and its Member States

kpi_list.kpi_text: The European Investment Bank funds (as of December 2022), EUR 3.47 billion to the SIDS, in the form of credit lines to local credit institutions to support SMEs, financing infrastructure investments, and in energy, services, health, education, agriculture and fisheries.
kpi_list.metric_name: European Investment Bank Funding to SIDS
kpi_list.target_description: Provide EUR 3.47 billion in credit lines and financing to support SMEs and infrastructure in SIDS
kpi_list.measurement_method: Financial disbursement and reporting of credit lines and investments

kpi_list.kpi_text: The EU is also funding a EUR 35 billion programme of support for African, Caribbean and Pacific SIDS and coastal countries, including the Biospace programme in the Caribbean, the Bioscape programme in the Pacific, and support to the Critical Ecosystems Partnership Fund in the Western Indian Ocean.
kpi_list.metric_name: EU Programme Funding for ACP SIDS and Coastal Countries
kpi_list.target_description: Fund a EUR 35 billion programme supporting SIDS and coastal countries in Africa, Caribbean and Pacific regions
kpi_list.measurement_method: Financial disbursement and programme implementation reports
kpi_list.responsible_entity: European Union and its Member States

kpi_list.kpi_text: The EU highlights the importance of achieving land degradation neutrality by 2030, and welcome COP16 to the UNCCD in Saudi Arabia as the moment for accelerating national and global action on land restoration, soil health, drought resilience and green transition.
kpi_list.target_description: Achieve land degradation neutrality by 2030 through accelerated national and global action on land restoration, soil health, drought resilience and green transition
kpi_list.measurement_method: Monitoring of land degradation indicators and progress reports from UNCCD and national governments
kpi_list.responsible_entity: EU Member States, National Governments, UNCCD

kpi_list.kpi_text: The EU will work closely with partners to accelerate and benefit from the green transition and support the implementation of global commitments. The EU is convinced of the potential of renewable energies, including marine renewable energies, for the ocean-based economy and other areas significant to sustainable development.
kpi_list.metric_name: Green Transition and Renewable Energy Implementation
kpi_list.target_description: Accelerate green transition and implement renewable energy solutions, including marine renewables, to support sustainable ocean-based economies
kpi_list.measurement_method: Implementation of renewable energy projects and progress towards green transition targets
kpi_list.responsible_entity: European Union and its Member States, SIDS partners

kpi_list.kpi_text: The EU and its Member States will continue to strengthen collaboration with partners in developing and implementing ambitious Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) that effectively address commitments taken in the GST, including economy-wide emission reduction targets aligned with limiting global warming to 1.5°C.
kpi_list.metric_name: NDC Implementation and Emission Reduction Alignment
kpi_list.target_description: Develop and implement ambitious NDCs with economy-wide emission reduction targets aligned with limiting global warming to 1.5°C
kpi_list.measurement_method: Review of NDC submissions and progress reports under the Global Stocktake (GST)
kpi_list.responsible_entity: European Union, Member States, SIDS partners

kpi_list.kpi_text: The EU welcomes the proposed Multidimensional Vulnerability Index (MVI) and calls for its swift endorsement... By collecting more and disaggregated data, the MVI should give greater understanding to inform decisions.
kpi_list.metric_name: Multidimensional Vulnerability Index Endorsement and Use
kpi_list.target_description: Swift endorsement and adoption of the MVI to better reflect vulnerabilities of SIDS and inform development decisions
kpi_list.measurement_method: Formal endorsement of MVI and integration into development institution analyses
kpi_list.responsible_entity: European Union, Development Institutions, SIDS partners

kpi_list.kpi_text: The EU recalls the importance of supporting the UN Secretary General’s call for the ‘Early Warnings for All’ initiative, in particular closing major data gaps for weather and climate observations from SIDS, ensuring that warnings are appropriate to local needs, and disseminating them to local populations.
kpi_list.metric_name: Early Warning Systems Enhancement for SIDS
kpi_list.target_description: Close data gaps for weather and climate observations, ensure locally appropriate warnings, and disseminate them effectively to local populations in SIDS
kpi_list.timeframe: ongoing with emphasis in 2024 and beyond
kpi_list.measurement_method: Assessment of data coverage, warning dissemination effectiveness, and local responsiveness
kpi_list.responsible_entity: European Union, UN, SIDS national authorities

kpi_list.kpi_text: The EU is committed to working closely with partners to accelerate and benefit from the green transition and support the implementation of global commitments.
kpi_list.metric_name: Support for Global Green Transition Commitments
kpi_list.target_description: Accelerate green transition efforts and support implementation of global environmental commitments in partnership with SIDS
kpi_list.measurement_method: Monitoring progress on green transition initiatives and global commitment adherence
kpi_list.responsible_entity: European Union and its Member States

kpi_list.kpi_text: The EU and its Member States support ongoing efforts to reform the International Financial Architecture and multilateral development banks, building on the roadmap of the Paris Pact for People and the Planet (4P) and the Bridgetown Agenda 2.0.
kpi_list.target_description: Support reform of international financial institutions to better address development needs of SIDS
kpi_list.timeframe: by 2025 (including Summit of the Future and 4th International Conference on Financing For Development)
kpi_list.measurement_method: Participation in reform discussions and implementation of agreed reforms
kpi_list.responsible_entity: European Union and its Member States

top_actors.name: European Union
top_actors.justification: The European Union is the primary actor throughout the document, frequently mentioned as the main partner and supporter of SIDS. It leads key initiatives, provides substantial funding, drives policy frameworks, and coordinates cooperation with multiple stakeholders, making it central to the text's themes.

top_actors.name: EU Member States
top_actors.justification: EU Member States are consistently referenced alongside the EU, jointly committing to actions, funding, and partnerships. Their role is crucial in implementing policies, supporting climate action, and engaging in multilateral negotiations, reflecting their significant influence and participation.

top_actors.name: United Nations
top_actors.justification: The United Nations is a key multilateral partner referenced in relation to global frameworks, summits, and resolutions that impact SIDS. It provides platforms for dialogue, policy development, and coordination, including specific UN offices and initiatives dedicated to SIDS, underscoring its importance.

top_themes.name: Multilateralism
top_themes.justification: Multilateralism is central to the document as it highlights the EU's commitment to working with international organizations, UN bodies, and SIDS partners to address climate change, sustainable development, and financing. The document repeatedly references UN summits, agreements, and multilateral frameworks, underscoring the strategic importance of collective global action.

top_themes.name: Global Digital Cooperation
top_themes.justification: Global Digital Cooperation is important as the EU emphasizes digital transformation as a key enabler for socio-economic development, climate action, and inclusion in SIDS. The document mentions initiatives like the Digital for Development Hub and stresses the need for equitable digital access and partnerships, linking digital cooperation to broader development goals.

top_themes.name: Digital Inclusion
top_themes.justification: Digital Inclusion is relevant as the document highlights the role of digitalization in promoting inclusive development, education, and overcoming remoteness challenges faced by SIDS. It is strategically important for ensuring vulnerable groups benefit from digital advances, supporting the EU’s broader commitments to social development and equity.
